cards.text: Welcome to the church at Antioch, friend! It's got a whole team of prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen and Saul. Five names on the roster, and one of them grew up with somebody you would NOT expect.

cards.question: Manaen, one of the teachers at Antioch, was brought up with somebody famous. Who?

cards.text: While they're worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit speaks, and He says to set apart two of these five for the work He's called them to. Ever hear the boss say your name in a meeting and feel your whole soul leave your body? THAT moment.

cards.question: The Holy Spirit tells the church at Antioch to set apart two of its five prophets and teachers. Which two?
After they fast and pray, the church lays its ___ on Barnabas and Saul and sends them off.

cards.text: Sent out by the Holy Spirit, Barnabas and Saul go down to Seleucia and set sail. When the Holy Spirit is the one sending you, friend, you do NOT argue about the window seat.

cards.question: From Seleucia, Barnabas and Saul sail to the island of ___.

cards.text: When they land at Salamis, they proclaim the word of God. Me? First thing I do anywhere new is hunt down an outlet for my phone.

cards.question: In Salamis, Barnabas and Saul proclaim the word of God in the Jewish ___.
On this trip to Cyprus, Barnabas and Saul travel with nobody else along.

cards.text: They travel the whole island as far as Paphos, and there they find a Jewish sorcerer and false prophet named Bar-Jesus. Sorcerer AND false prophet, friend, that's two titles on one business card, and neither one is good news.

cards.question: Bar-Jesus is an attendant of the proconsul Sergius Paulus, a man of intelligence. Why does the proconsul call for Barnabas and Saul?

answers.text: He wants to hear the word of God
He wants them off his island
He wants them put under arrest

cards.question: Bar-Jesus, also called Elymas the sorcerer, backs up Barnabas and Saul in front of the proconsul.

cards.text: Nope, Elymas opposes them and tries to turn the proconsul from the faith. Then Saul, filled with the Holy Spirit, looks right at him, and it's the kind of look that makes a grown man put his phone DOWN.

cards.question: Saul goes by another name too. He's also called ___.

cards.text: Paul doesn't hold back, calling Elymas a “child of the devil and enemy of all righteousness” who's full of deceit and trickery. I've had an oven timer yell at me for ten straight minutes, and it NEVER got that specific.

cards.question: Paul tells Elymas the hand of the Lord is against him. What does Paul say will happen to Elymas?

answers.text: He will be blind for a time
He will lose his voice for a time
He will be driven out of Paphos

cards.text: Immediately, mist and darkness come over Elymas. He gropes around, looking for someone to lead him by the hand.

cards.question: After the proconsul Sergius Paulus sees what happened to Elymas, he sends Barnabas and Saul away.

cards.text: Sergius Paulus believes, astonished at the teaching about the Lord. Hold that thought, friend, because Barnabas and Paul have a LOT more road in front of them.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: the Holy Spirit's line, the boss question, and "THAT moment." Only the opening card can go past two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "THAT moment" says Barnabas and Saul felt dread when they were named, as if it were fact. The text gives no feeling here. Papa Dorin doesn't mark it as his own guess.

rule.text: Feelings. He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: The question says the Holy Spirit "tells the church at Antioch." Acts 13:2 only says "the Holy Spirit said" while "they" were worshiping, so who He spoke to stays open. Naming the church as the listener goes beyond the text.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The question says "the church lays its ___ on Barnabas and Saul." Acts 13:3 only says "they laid their hands on them." The text doesn't say who "they" are, so making it the church fills in what the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: "When they land...", "Me?" and "First thing I do...".

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke gives Papa Dorin a phone and a habit of traveling to new places. His story is the Millers' kitchen, the drawer and a cookie planet just big enough for his bakery. This adds something new to his world that isn't a habit around his bakery.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: John (Acts 13:5) is never named or introduced. Card 10 only asks whether anyone else came along. The baker never learns that John was with Barnabas and Saul as their helper, and nothing says who he is.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."
